#6860. The Real-Life Diet of Christian McCaffrey, Who Thinks Cold Plunges Are a Metaphor for Life

The last time Christian McCaffrey was featured in this magazine, in 2020, he posed poolside, ogling the camera in nothing but a pair of crisp white Calvin Kleins. The All-Pro running back still looks like Adonis, but a lot has changed in six years. For one, he's a 49er now, and at the midway point of the 2026 NFL season he and quarterback Brock Purdy, a popular MVP candidate, have San Francisco sitting pretty atop the NFC. McCaffrey, now in his 11th NFL season, also recently became a father, a development that's thrown the demands of professional football into stark relief. “I want to spend all day with my kids,” he confesses. “But obviously I play football, so it's not always like that.”

When McCaffrey's not chasing after his springy 15-month old daughter, his days consist of morning prayer ("it puts me in the right head space"), film study (he goes through “a bunch of notebooks every year”), cold plunges ("a good metaphor for life, actually"), and meditation, a practice he embraced this past summer under the auspices of the movement coordinator and spiritual guru Ido Portal. “Some days were great,” McCaffrey says. “Some days were crippling.”

But the week we spoke, the 49ers happened to be on their bye, which meant the typically scrupulous 30-year-old could permit himself that rare indulgence: a slice of his wife Olivia Culpo's carrot cake.

Christian McCaffrey: It's funny, even on the bye week, you can never just take a week off. You always have to do something. For me, you get a good week in the middle of the season to just get your body back, get your mind back. I think a lot of it is just being with my family. It's so good for your mind, your body, your soul. And then in the mornings, I'll do whatever workout—the team gives us different workouts to do throughout the week so that you stay up to date or you're at least moving a little bit. And then recovery work, any treatment you have to do, and later in the afternoon you'll do another mobility recovery session just to stay moving so you don't get stale.

I think the first thing that I did right was marry correctly. When you play in the NFL, it just takes all of your energy and time, frankly. I mean, I want to spend all day with my kids, but obviously I play football too, so it's not always like that. So to be able to still do my job and know that they're taken care of—my wife's a super mom, so I still do everything I need to do. And when you come home, to be able to look at my daughter's face and hold my son and just spend time with them, it makes those moments so much better.

My son is a month old, but my daughter—she's 14, 15 months now, and she's all over the place. If there's something to play with, she'll play with it. She is obsessed with that little Roomba. She won't stop. She'll just click the button on the Roomba 24/7, and then when it starts moving, she gets scared and runs to me. She likes climbing and moving, and we just try to keep her moving as much as possible, and she loves it. Just watching her smile and enjoy life is the greatest thing ever.

For me, the staples are nutrition. Those are things you can control, always. So if I'm eating healthy, if I'm getting the correct amount of sleep, if I have my Dymatize shake after my workout or my prehab session or whatever it is, getting those positive calories into your system at the same times every day is something everybody can control. That's why partnering with them was easy for me, because it was a product that actually helped me and also tastes good.

I like the Fruity Pebbles. I'm still a kid at heart, so anything that tastes like an old cereal, I'm going to go ahead and do that. But I mean, there's so many things out there now. It's almost overwhelming how many modalities and recovery tools and different things you can do. But I think the thing I've learned most, as somebody that's experimented with all of that stuff, is your mindset and your ability to just stay moving is critical. I think you can try all of the different tools, but if you're not doing the staples—moving, recovering from moving, eating correctly, having the right nutrition, sleeping correctly—then a lot of this stuff is not going to move the needle as much as you think.

I used to, and then I got way too obsessed over it. But I had an Oura ring for a long time, and I'll track my sleep in the offseason with that.

Well, it's fascinating. After the season, you think you're sleeping well, but your body and your mind go through a lot over an NFL season. So you think, “Oh, I can rest now.” But I was looking at the sleep scores early in the offseason and they were horrible. Maybe I slept eight hours, but it's the worst sleep ever. You're detoxing… I mean, the reality is that you take a lot of drugs to help you play. You have to do all these things to help you get back on the field on Sunday, with all the hits you're taking. So it takes a while to get back to a good sleep score. But then once I get the ball rolling it’s like, "Okay, I'm in a good place now.”

I don't think anyone loves getting into the cold plunge. But everyone loves it after. The cold plunge is a good metaphor for life, actually. The things that are usually the most challenging are usually the most beneficial. So yeah, I've learned to like it. And again, when you're playing and it's in season, you're so focused on the practice and the game and getting your body right that the things that you think just become routine and habit.

I always start my morning with prayer. That's been a staple, and if I can connect with God as much as possible, it just puts me in the right head space. It reminds me why I'm doing this and it eliminates a lot of distractions. I meditated a lot this offseason, especially in the summer. I worked with a guy, Ido Portal, who's a legend and has had a massive influence on me. And for six weeks straight, we did one hour of stillness every morning. That was a huge challenge, but a really moving experience. I still do that all the time. I don't have time to do it for an hour anymore, but if I can get 20 minutes in the mornings, or even throughout the day at a random point where I have a little window, I try to do that as much as possible. That just helps your nervous system get back to where it's supposed to be, especially in a high-stress week.

Yeah, I'd never done that before until this summer. And Ido, he's a character, man, but he's a beautiful person and an unbelievable human being. It was very moving working with him for a summer, and it wasn't negotiable. We were doing it, starting at seven o'clock every morning, one hour straight, complete stillness, can't move, nothing. It's only something you can explain through experience. It wasn't about whether or not you turned your brain off. There was no shot. For six weeks, I didn't shut my brain off one time. It's more about, can you focus and refocus on the task at hand as best as possible? Some days were great. Some days were crippling. Some days you're cramping because you're in a seated crisscross position and you're like, "I'm in so much pain." And then you get done and you're like, "Wait a second, I wasn't in as much pain as I thought." It was such a moving experience because, again, you said you were going to do something, therefore you need to do it. You're going to find out what your purpose is through this six-week experience. It might be different than the guy next to you. It might be different than Ido's, but you're going to go through it, and you're going to learn a lot about yourself and you'll be better for it.

You watch so much film with the team all the time, but people think we just go out and practice and play. But really, we have a job. We're sitting in meetings taking notes all day. I mean, you go through a bunch of notebooks every year in the NFL and you're watching film all the time. I've watched less film as I've gotten older, but I'll watch a lot of blitz tape to make sure I'm prepared for different tells, when they're blitzing, when they're not. But running back is such an instinctual position, so I try to train the instinct more than predict things based on what you're seeing. There are certain things you can pick up on, but that can also be a crutch, so I try to find the middle ground.

Look, I try to eat as clean as possible, but there's a time to indulge. If you're feeling great and you have a couple of days off—if my wife's going to make a dessert, I'm going to eat it. It's good for the soul.

She makes a carrot cake and, to this day, there's not a better one I've had. Or my mom will be in town and cook something. Or her mom will be in town and cook something. So I'll definitely indulge every once in a while, but throughout the week I eat clean.

#6859. Breaking Down ‘Love Island USA’ Alum Kay Kay and Kassy’s Friendship Fallout Over Johnny

Wondering how Daniela and Andrea are also involved? It’s confusing.

The best thing about Love Island USA: The drama doesn’t end when the Islanders leave the Villa. In fact, Islanders can make headlines years after the fact, as evidenced by the fact that season 5’s Vickala “Kay Kay” Gray and Kassandra “Kassy” Castillo are currently engaged in a heated online battle...and reportedly, it revolves around season 2’s Johnny Middlebrooks. Confused? Same! So let’s break it down.

It all (seemingly) began in September, when Kay Kay posted a TikTok talking about how “friendship breakups low-key hurt way more than regular relationship breakups.” She didn’t name any names, but fans couldn’t help but notice that she hadn’t been posting with her bestie Kassy as frequently...and the two seemingly no longer followed each other.

But it wasn’t until November that things really heated up. Starting with...

On November 5, Daniela Ortiz (who became friends with Kassy when she appeared as a Bombshell on season 6) got involved, posting a (since-deleted) TikTok in which she calls out people who act like victims despite being in the wrong.

Names are not mentioned, but fans jump to the conclusion that—just like with Kay Kay—she’s talking about Kassy.

Not long after, season 6 alum Andrea Carmona enters the chat, taking to TikTok to tell a story that’s seemingly about an interaction with Kassy at an October 2025 Celsius event (though once again, the name “Kassy” is never mentioned)...and Andrea seemingly accuses Kassy of hitting on her boyfriend, Matt Dubost (aka DJ Acaze).

The video has since been deleted, but of course, the internet has receipts.

Kassy posted a TikTok in response to Andrea’s story, saying she isn’t sure where these rumors started, but she never came on to Andrea’s boyfriend at the Celsius event.

“I want you to know I didn’t say anything,” she said, adding, “I didn’t try to ever disrespect you or your partner, and I’m sorry that you believed I did.”

In response to a fan who asks, “Why does this need to be public...like text her,” Andrea posted a response TikTok (which, again, has been deleted) with text reading, “She slept with the guy her best friend was hooking up with then lied about it when confronted. So why would I reach out? We all unfollowed her for a reason.”

Andrea also dropped a comment reading, “ALSO DISCLAIMER: I got permission from the friend to speak on this bc she over it too.”

Which of course has everyone asking, “Which friend? Which guy?”

Finally, names are names. Kassy posted a second TikTok, where she (1) calls out Andrea for getting involved in a situation that doesn’t involve her, (2) shares that she and Kay Kay are no longer friends, and (3) reveals that it’s because she had a “one-night stand” with season 2’s Johnny while he was hooking up with Kay Kay.

Oh, and about her fallout with Daniela? It apparently had to do with a confessional from the Unwell Summer Games (on which Kassy and Daniela both appeared), where Kassy admitted to “kind of stealing her man” when asked about her relationship with Daniela.

According to Kassy, that comment was made in reference to Rob Rausch and it was very much meant to be a joke...but apparently, Daniela didn’t take it that way!

Kay Kay commented on Kassy’s second video, writing, “Kassy we both know this has so little to do with a man and everything to do with the betrayal of our friendship.”

In response, Kassy apologized for taking the drama online but pointed out that Andrea posted about it first and “mentioned she got approval” to talk about the situation from Kay Kay.

Andrea posted her third (and, hopefully, final) TikTok about the drama, alleging that “there are four other girls I can name that were quote unquote your friends that you have intentionally went for their ex-boyfriend or their current situationship.”

After sliding into Kassy’s TikTok comments to write, “This was just the tipping point” and “everyone has their own stories to tell about you,” Daniela posts yet another TikTok, saying, “I have my own reasons for not being friends with Kassy. They have nothing to do with this whatsoever.”

Following Daniela’s second video, fans decide to slide into season 5 alum Johnnie Garcia’s comments to ask what her reason was for ending her friendship with Kassy, as people had noticed that they were seemingly no longer friends as well.

Johnnie’s response? She said her reason “had nothing to do with Kay Kay” and that her and Kassy’s “friendship ended many months ago.”

In her third TikTok, Kassy asked fans for grace, saying she just “wants this to stop” and that she “did not sign up for this.”

At long last, Kay Kay broke her silence with a nearly 18-minute-long video (!!), basically saying that the problem isn’t about Kassy sleeping with Johnny but the way Kassy went about doing so, since Kay Kay claims Kassy actively pursued Johnny.

Oh, and when asked why she wasn’t willing to accept Kassy’s apology, Kay Kay posted a second video, saying that Kassy only apologized to fans, not to Kay Kay herself.

Kay Kay also revealed that Kassy allegedly slept with season 6’s Connor Newsum, despite her friendship with his ex, Carmen Kocourek.

Most recently, Johnny entered the discourse with a video reading, “POV: Me preparing for my Netflix documentary on why I’m always the villain.”

#6856. ‘Off Campus’ Season 2 Finally Has a Release Date—And It’s Sooner Than You Think

I didn’t expect to get into a soapy college-set romance this summer, but here we are—and I’m not the only one. Off Campus, based on the Elle Kennedy book series of the same name, has swiftly become a runaway success; the Prime Video show is now the third most-watched debut series of all time on the streamer, with a combined 36 million viewers in its first two weeks.

It’s easy to see why. Like all the best teen dramas of yore, it exists within the comforting, color-saturated world of jocks and college parties, of red cups and romances, diners and karaoke bars. Nothing really dark ever happens, it’s only ever alluded to; and you can be sure that despite any setbacks these characters may face, they’ll all work it out in the end.

Amazon already knew it was going to be a doozy. Off Campus was renewed for a second season back in February, months before the first season even premiered. But what can we expect from the second horny ice hockey drama of the last year, which now has an official premiere date? Here’s what we know about Season 2.

Off Campus’s first season focused on a blossoming romance between ice hockey star Garrett Graham (Belmont Cameli) and bookish music student Hannah Wells (Ella Bright). But, as with each book, each season will likely focus on a different love story, meaning Garrett and Hannah won’t be the central couple of Season 2.

In an Instagram teaser, Amazon confirmed that Season 2 would primarily focus on Hannah’s best friend Allie (Mika Abdalla) and Garrett’s ice hockey pal Dean (Stephen Kalyn), who spent Season 1 in a “friends with benefits” situation that started to feel serious.

“We are so excited to continue Allie and Dean’s story as our primary romance of season two,” Off Campus writer Louisa Levy said in a statement. “But if you fell in love with Hannah and Garrett, don’t worry—they will still be an integral part of our robust ensemble. We’re looking forward to telling the next chapter of everyone’s story. There’s a lot for fans to look forward to!”

The streamer has confirmed that plenty of the Season 1 cast are carrying on into the next season (Bright as Hannah, Cameli as Garrett, Abdalla as Allie, Kalyn as Dean, Antonio Cipriano as John Logan and Jalen Thomas Brooks as John Tucker).

But there will also be some new faces. On April 30, India Fowler (White Lines, Insomnia) was announced as Grace Ivers for Season 2 (the eagle-eyed among us will have noticed that she did make a minor cameo in the first season at the Hawks’ fundraiser event at Malone’s. And, well, spoiler—Ivers appears as Logan’s love interest in the book series). Phillipa Soo (Hamilton), will also join as Scarlett, a theatre artist who guest-directs an original play for Briar University’s drama department.

On August 14, Shay Rudolph (The Baby-Sitters Club) was also announced as Summer Di Laurentis, sister to the new season’s co-lead, Dean (Kalyn). If you don’t know who that is, she’s the main character in Kennedy’s U Briar book series, a spin-off from Off Campus (I know, there’s a lot to keep up with—Kennedy has written, I kid you not, upwards of 60 books).

One character that won’t be returning is Justin, played by Josh Heuston. “I love Josh, and I would not write him off if I can find a way to bring Justin back at some point,” Levy told TV Guide. “We never got a chance to meet Stella, who is the person he ends up with in the book. So maybe we’ll find a way to fold him into a future season. We don’t have him [available] next season, but never say never.”

Filming commenced on June 1, 2026. Last year, filming also began in June, and wrapped up in October. And as per Variety and confirmed by Amazon, Off Campus Season 2 finally has a release date—the YA drama will debut on 28 April, 2027. So, even sooner than our initial predictions of May. Siri, play “Life Is Worth Living” by Justin Bieber.

In the meantime: why not binge Sterling Point, another cozy drama that’ll have you oddly invested in the love lives of some fictional teens?

#6855. What to Wear to an Interview for Every Industry and Budget

Looking for a job can be a grueling marathon of resumes, cover letters, and HR acronyms—and that’s before you ever get into the room with your would-be future employer (or their AI proxy, as may be the case). Once you’ve secured an interview, the finish line may feel tantalizingly close, but the race is far from over. Before you get the chance to wow them with your articulate and highly considered insights into your personal strengths, weaknesses, career goals, and salary expectations, however, you’ve got to make a good first impression, and that starts with what you wear. So what, exactly, should one wear to a job interview in 2026? Aside from “probably not pajama pants,” the right answer depends on the job. Despite the loosening of office dress codes across the board in recent years and the rise of remote work in the post-pandemic era, every industry has its own answer to that question, from the traditional suit and tie to “whatever makes you feel the most creative.” For advice on getting the right look for the job, we consulted a bunch of folks who ought to know.

“The interview and the job are very different things,” explains Atlanta-based personal stylist Joshua Davis. “A tech founder might wear a T-shirt to a meeting with a VC, but even if all your research says the office is pretty casual, you should still go more conservative for the interview.” Davis suggests researching the company on LinkedIn to see how employees present themselves and even perusing their individual social media accounts for further insights into their style and presentation. “People expect that a lawyer will arrive in an E-Class and wear a black suit. A trial attorney might, but an attorney who specializes in tech IP will usually dress more like their client,” he adds. “The same is true for most bankers, consultants, and accountants who are client-facing – they have learned to research their client and make sure their image is usually only slightly more conservative than the person they are trying to sell to.”

Whether you’re applying at a disruptive startup or a firm with centuries of history, your clothes are an important means of determining how well you’ll fit into the corporate culture and represent the company to the world. “We get a fair number of calls from HR departments that have found a great candidate, but they don’t feel like they can fully recommend that person because of their wardrobe,” Davis says. “The most common reason is that a candidate is dressing too casually or they don’t dress for their body. To translate, that means too sloppy or too sexy.”

At the most formal end of the spectrum are law firms, and the longer a firm has been around the more traditional its dress code is likely to be. “Law firms in New York are still conservative workplaces and interviewees hoping to land a position as an attorney should still wear a suit with leather shoes,” says Jessica Chin Somers, Esq., a managing director at Kinney Recruiting, an NYC-based legal recruiter. “For men, the uniform of a blue suit with brown shoes or a gray suit with black shoes exists for a reason, but more important than color is the fit.” Aside from that, Chin says, there’s only one big rule to remember: “Lawyers do not show up to interviews wearing sneakers, no matter how “cool” you think the firm is or how expensive the shoes.”

Unless it’s a firm specializing in crypto, the finance field’s dress code remains similarly conservative. “First impressions are important, especially for a job interview in the finance industry, and the candidate needs to convey a sense of seriousness, competence, and trustworthiness,” explains J. Daniel Chi, Ph.D., the chair of the finance department at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. “The dress code has relaxed quite a bit over recent years, however, as a job candidate, unless the firm gives clear instructions on dressing casually, dressing formally is a safer bet.”

The tech world’s reputation for preferring hoodies and sneakers over suits and brogues turns out to be well deserved. “What I see with a lot of different [tech] companies is a more casual approach to being at the office,” says Sam Fricker, the head of recruiting at Philo, a streaming service with offices in the Bay Area. “Because our company is bi-coastal, employees who are based on the East Coast sometimes are sometimes dressed more formally,” adds Maryland-based Philo Recruiter Alexis Fagin. “Departments may differ as well, like finance teams might require a little bit more of a buttoned-up look for meetings, for example.”

At Toast, a tech company serving the restaurant industry, things are similarly relaxed. “We encourage employees to wear whatever makes them feel most comfortable and confident to do their jobs, and the same goes for those interviewing,” says Toast's chief people officer Mike Gutner. “That said, our recruiters will suggest something in the realm of business casual. The bulk of our interviews are virtual at this point, so I’m sure I’ve talked to more than a couple of applicants in formal tops who are also wearing sweatpants and slippers below the camera. I won’t blame them; I do the same from time to time.”

At the other end of the spectrum are creative agencies, whose commitment to out-of-the-box thinking extends to personal presentation. “[Your] experience and portfolio far outweigh [your] presentation,” says Matt Johnson, the founder and chief strategy officer of LA-based creative agency Haymaker. “At the end of the day, we’re investing in the person and their abilities, not their appearance, so I’d say dress to represent your best and most true self. The more authentic you can be, the better.”

“NGOs value humility and authentic alignment with the cause, and your outfit should communicate authenticity, cultural sensitivity, and reliability,” says Sam DeMase, a career expert at ZipRecruiter in NYC. In other words, the safest play at your NGO interview is business casual, i.e. a blazer and button-up shirt with trousers or dark jeans, or a sweater, a collared shirt, and dress pants or chinos. Depending on the role and the organization, you should also steer clear of anything too flashy or obviously expensive-looking, the better to reinforce your focus on the mission.

Jobs in media—a range that covers everything from journalism to social media management to advertising planning—are extremely diverse, as are the dress codes at media organizations, but most media companies fall on the more casual end of the spectrum. “You want to wear something you feel genuinely comfortable in so you can focus on the conversation and be yourself,” advises Rich Kleiman, the CEO and co-founder of Boardroom, a sports, business, and entertainment network. “But comfort shouldn’t come at the expense of fit. Whatever you wear, make sure it fits well and feels intentional.” Despite this latitude, Kleiman cautions against confusing casual with careless, and advises investing in alterations to nail the fit. “Sometimes, investing a little in your presentation is worth it, especially if it helps you walk into the room feeling confident.”

Dress codes can vary widely between academic institutions and the departments within them, so the best course of action is to act like an academic and do your research, says Jocelyn Coalter, senior director of career and leadership development at St. John’s University in NYC. Beyond that, she advises candidates to err on the side of formality when in doubt. “It’s a lot easier to remove a blazer that you may not need than to put one on that you didn't bring,” she says. “I also recommend professional yet comfortable shoes for academic interviews, as there’s often a component that involves meeting different people on different parts of campus, or getting a tour.”

#6854. All About Luciana Damon, Matt Damon’s Wife of More Than 20 Years

Matt Damon may be one of Hollywood’s biggest stars, but his love story started far from a movie set.

The actor met his wife, Luciana Damon (née Barroso), in 2003 while filming Stuck on You in Miami. At the time, she was a bartender, and what began as an unexpected meeting eventually grew into a long-lasting marriage.

More than two decades later, the couple shares four daughters, has worked together professionally behind the scenes, and continues to make family a priority—even as Matt’s career takes him around the world. Most recently, Luciana and their daughters joined him at the London and New York premieres of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey.

Here’s everything to know about Luciana Damon.

Luciana was born in Argentina and later moved to the United States.

While she has largely stayed out of the public eye throughout her marriage, she gave a rare interview to Vogue Australia in 2018, offering a glimpse into her family life and relationship with Matt.

Matt and Luciana first crossed paths in 2003 while he was filming Stuck on You in Miami.

Matt has often described it as love at first sight. During a 2011 appearance on The Ellen DeGeneres Show, he recalled, “I literally saw her across a crowded room, literally. Eight years and four kids later, that’s my life. I don’t know how else our paths would’ve crossed if that didn’t happen.”

Luciana remembers the evening a little differently.

“Matt’s story is that he saw me across the room, and there was a light on me. And I’m like, ‘Yeah, it was a nightclub—there were lights everywhere!’” she told Vogue Australia.

She explained that Matt came behind the bar after fans began approaching him for photos and autographs.

“He had started getting recognized and asked for pictures and autographs, and then it got kind of aggressive because people are drinking and stuff,” she said. “So he came and hid behind the bar...[wanting to] just hang out back there and have a drink. He says, ‘Oh, I saw you, and I really wanted to talk to you.’”

Rather than letting him stand around, she gave him a job.

“I said: ‘You know, if you’re going to be back here, you can’t just be standing there!’” she recalled. “He had trained as a bartender for a film years before, so he started making drinks. And he made me a ton of money in tips that night, because of course everyone wanted to go and see him. So it turned into a really fun night and then 15 years later, here we are!”

Luciana was raising her daughter, Alexia, from a previous relationship when she met Matt.

She told Vogue Australia that when Matt invited her to continue the evening with him and his friends, she declined because she needed to get home.

“I was like, ‘I can’t, I have a four-year-old daughter, I’m not going anywhere’...and that was one of the things he loved, that I had a daughter,” she said.

“He said, ‘I love that you’re a mom and that’s your priority.’ Some guys might have been different, they might think it’s complicated, but for him it wasn’t. When you meet somebody that you have a connection with, that’s just the person that you have a connection with, all the other stuff—the movie-star part—wasn’t really a factor. It was just Matt, to me he’s just Matt.”

The couple later welcomed three daughters together—Isabella, Gia, and Stella—and Matt has long considered Alexia his own daughter as well.

After dating for roughly two years, Matt and Luciana married in a private ceremony in December 2005.

Their wedding bands carry a particularly meaningful family tradition. Speaking to Parade in 2017, Matt explained that the rings contain tiny diamonds from his grandparents’ wedding ring.

“They weren’t quality diamonds; it was what [my grandfather] could afford,” he said. “But the marriage lasted. They were married for over 60 years. It wasn’t about the ring; it was about the marriage.”

“So when I told my mother that I was marrying Lucy, she gave me that ring and there were these six little diamonds. We took three of them and we put them on the inside of my band, and then we took three and we put them on the inside of her band. So they’re not visible, but we’re hopefully carrying the best part of that union with us.”

Over the years, Matt has shared one relationship rule that has helped their marriage endure.

“We have a two-week rule,” he told YourTango in 2021. “I’m not away for more than two weeks. I think you need to be with the person you love as much as possible. My wife is my soulmate. I don’t like being apart from her.”

There have been rare exceptions. While promoting Oppenheimer in 2023, Matt joked to Entertainment Weekly that he negotiated a break from acting with one exception.

“I had—not to get too personal—negotiated extensively with my wife that I was taking time off,” he said. “The one caveat to my taking time off was if Chris Nolan called.”

Matt has repeatedly credited Luciana with helping him navigate both his career and life.

During an interview with Jake’s Takes in 2023, he recalled feeling discouraged while filming a movie that wasn’t turning out the way he’d hoped.

“I remember my wife pulling me up because I fell into a depression,” he said.

Matt added, “I do pride myself, in a large part because of her, at being a professional actor. And what being a professional actor means is you go and you do the 15-hour day and give it absolutely everything, even in what you know is going to be a losing effort. If you can do that with the best possible attitude, then you’re a pro. And she really helped me with that.”

Although Luciana wasn’t part of the entertainment industry when she met Matt, she’s taken on a larger role behind the camera in recent years.

She served as an executive producer on The Instigators in 2024 and produced The Rip in 2026.

Speaking with Entertainment Tonight at The Instigators premiere, Matt said the producing credit had been years in the making.

“She’s been reading every script and watching every cut of every movie for 21 years. This is the first time we ever kind of codified it,” he said.

He added that Luciana initially resisted taking credit for her work.

“She didn’t even want to take the credit. She was there every day, she was doing all this work on the script, and then she was like, ‘Nah, I don’t want to take the credit.’”

“The other producers on the movie...came of their own volition [and said], ‘If you’re not taking credit, we’re not taking credit.’ It was very sweet. She succumbed and took the credit.”

Luciana has rarely spoken publicly about her marriage, but when Vogue Australia asked about the secret to a lasting relationship, her answer was refreshingly simple.

“I just know I think we both feel, really, really lucky to have met each other so we don’t take that for granted. It’s life and marriage, so there’s ups and downs you know, but overall it’s easy and it’s fun. And he’s such a good dad.”

In a November 2026 interview with GQ, Matt revealed that Luciana underwent brain surgery after experiencing a brain aneurysm in 2024.

“She’s totally fine, thank God, but [she] had this brain surgery the week before the Oscars,” he said.

Although the couple missed the ceremony, Luciana surprised Matt by getting dressed up to attend an Oscars after-party once she was feeling better.

“But it was the first night she felt good enough to get up and had her energy back. And she surprised me and got a dress and we went out to the after-party, because she remembered that the last time it happened, I didn’t do it. And she was like, ‘This time we’re going out.’ And it was pretty fucking heroic of her to do that and really meaningful,” Damon recalled.

#6853. Meet the ‘Black Doves’ Season 2 Cast and Characters

New assassins! New spies! New... [redacted], we guess??

The spy series Black Doves is back for a second season after two years, dropping all at once, on Guy Fawkes Day of all days, November 5. Need a refresher before you dive back into the Netflix series? Here’s everything you need to know about the new and returning cast of Black Doves season 2. Some of the new characters are such big secrets, we actually don’t have any details yet. Exciting!!

The first season, set at Christmas time, followed a politician’s wife with a double life as a spy in a covert organization called the Black Doves. When the man she was having an affair with is murdered, her handler calls in an assassin and old friend of hers for protection. The two investigate her lover’s death and discover that he was part of something bigger and more dangerous than they knew. Obviously the second season will up the already sky-high stakes, and introduce new threats. That also means new characters and cast members. So let’s get into it!

Helen is a spy who “happens” to be married to a prominent conservative politician.

Keira Knightley had a dual breakout in Hollywood in 2002 with Bend it Like Beckham and then, the next year, with Love Actually. Shortly thereafter she starred in Pirates of the Caribbean and Pride & Prejudice. The latter earned her her first Academy Award nominated. She was nominated again in 2014 for The Imitation Game and has two BAFTA nominations, for that and for Atonement. She was also nominated for an Olivier after starring in The Misanthrope on the West End. Other credits include King Arthur, Never Let Me Go, Domino, The Duchess, Anna Karenina, Colette, and Begin Again.

Ben Whishaw has played two of the most iconic characters in the British canon: the Q to Daniel Craig’s James Bond, and Paddington himself. He is an Emmy and Golden Globe winner for A Very British Scandal, a BAFTA winner for that and This Is Going To Hurt, and a SAG nominee for Women Talking. Other credits include The Hours, Perfume: The Story of a Murderer, Brideshead Revisited, Bright Star, Cloud Atlas, Lilting, The Lobster, Mary Poppins Returns, Fargo, Passages, and Peter Hujar’s Day.

Sarah Lancashire is an acclaimed UK actress who appeared on over 500 episodes of Coronation Street. She was on Happy Valley for three seasons, and became an executive producer on the third. You might also know her from Last Tango in Halifax, Julia, Where the Heart Is, and The Paradise. She is also a stage actress with credits on the West End including Blood Brothers, Little Shop of Horrors, Guys and Dolls, and Betty Blue Eyes.

Helen’s husband Webb was the Secretary of Defence in season 1 and is now Prime Minister.

Andrew Buchan played Felim Bichan in the first two seasons of Industry and Andrew Parker Bowles in seasons 3 and 4 of The Crown. You might also remember him as Latimer on the first three seasons of Broadchurch. His other credits include Carnival Row, This England, The Spanish Princess, and All The Money in the World.

Williams is a mercenary with a grudge against Sam.

Ella Lily Hyland starred alongside Aidan Turner in Fifteen-Love back in 2023. Her other credits include A Thousand Blows and Towards Zero. You can see her next in the ensemble series Tall Tales & Murder.

Eleanor is also a mercenary and Williams’ partner.

Gabrielle Creevy has been a series regular on several television shows, including In My Skin, The Pact, Three Women, The Guest, and Amadeus in addition to Black Doves. She will star in the upcoming supernatural series The Witch Farm and also had a supporting role in the 2021 film Operation Mincemeat.

Neve Campbell is a Canadian actress best known for playing Sidney Prescott in the Scream franchise. Before that, she broke through with leading roles in the series Party of Five and the film The Craft. Since then, Campbell had leading or recurring roles on shows like Medium, The Philanthropist, Grey’s Anatomy, Welcome to Sweden, Manhattan, House of Cards, and The Lincoln Lawyer. Campbell is also the voice of Simba and Nala’s daughter Kiara in The Lion King 2: Simba’s Pride.

Ambika Mod is a comedian and actor you might know from television shows like This Is Going to Hurt, One Day, The Stolen Girl, and I Hate Suzie. On the big screen, she was recently in Black Bag and Sacrifice. (And her Halloween costume this year was Bend it Like Beckham, which ofc starred Knightley.)

Babou Ceesay recently received critical acclaim for playing the antihero Morrow in Alien: Earth on FX. He played Pilgrim on Into the Badlands. He’s set to appear in the second season of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms. His other television credits include Shardlake, Wolfe, and We Hunt Together. His film credits include Rogue One, Free Fire, and Resurrection.

Patrick works for an unknown, new organization, and offers to help Sam.

Sam Riley starred in the 2012 adaptation of Jack Kerouac’s novel On the Road. You might know him as Mr. Darcy, NBD, in Pride and Prejudice and Zombies. Riley played a raven in Maleficent and received critical acclaim for Control. His other credits include the 2020 Rebecca, Brighton Rock, and Free Fire.

There are three other new cast members this season. Sylvia Hoeks and Goran Kostic play Katia and Alexi Chernov. You’ve seen them before in Ride or Die and Jack Ryan, respectively. Plus, two-time Tony Award-nominated actor Samuel Barnett, who you may remember from Dirk Gently’s Holistic Detective Agency and who is currently starring in the musical Pride in London, plays the mysterious character “Jerry” this season. And finally, three more returning cast members in Black Doves season 2 are Kathryn Hunter as Sam’s old boss Lenny Lines, Agnes O’Casey as Helen’s assistant Dani, and Molly Chesworth as Helen’s nanny (and Reed’s daughter!!) Marie.
